mentions.name: 1e4.ai
mentions.description: A transformer-based (but not LLM) chess model that plays like a human, playable at 1e4.ai. It combines three models: a move model for choosing moves, a clock model that emulates human-like thinking time (inference itself takes milliseconds), and a winner model that predicts percentage-based likelihoods of white win / black win / draw rather than centipawn-based eval bars. The current model is trained on 1700-1800 rated Lichess games and can be tuned up or down, with training underway on a wide variety of other rating ranges; the site is rudimentary, offering play only (no saving or reviewing games). It is similar to MAIA, with slightly higher move prediction accuracy than the published MAIA-2 results.
mentions.problem: Typical chess engines don't play like humans, and standard eval bars show centipawn advantage rather than percentage-based game outcome likelihoods.
mentions.audience: Gamers and chess players looking for a human-like computer chess opponent.
